version: 2.1

parameters:
  setup_go:
    type: string
    default: github.com/circleci-functions/setup-go@v0.5.1-684fd5b

commands:
  setup:
    steps:
      - checkout
      - install-go
      - install-task

  # Installs the toolchain and restores the module, build and lint caches, saved at job end.
  install-go:
    steps:
      - run: circleci run << pipeline.parameters.setup_go >> --
          --version-file go.mod
          --golangci-lint-cache
          --checksum '{{ checksum "go.sum" }}_{{ checksum "clikit/go.sum" }}_{{ checksum "tools/go.sum" }}'
      - run: go version

  install-task:
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Install go-task
          command: |
            sh -c "$(curl --location https://taskfile.dev/install.sh)" -- -d -b "$HOME/.local/bin"
            echo 'export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"' >> "$BASH_ENV"

  # GoReleaser's dockers_v2 pipe shells out to `docker buildx build`, so the
  # builder and the registry login have to exist before it runs.
  setup-docker:
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Register QEMU for cross-architecture builds
          # Dockerfile.alpine RUNs `apk add`, once per platform in the manifest,
          # so building its arm64 half on an amd64 host needs binfmt handlers
          # registered. Idempotent, and a no-op for the cimg/base image, which
          # only COPYs.
          command: docker run --privileged --rm tonistiigi/binfmt --install arm64
      - run:
          name: Create a buildx builder
          # The machine image's default buildx driver is `docker`, which can
          # neither build for two platforms in one invocation nor push a
          # manifest list. A docker-container driver can do both.
          command: docker buildx create --use --driver docker-container
      - run:
          name: Log in to Docker Hub
          # Absent on branch dry-runs, which have no context: the snapshot build
          # still exercises the Dockerfile, it just pushes nothing.
          command: |
            if [ -z "${DOCKER_HUB_USERNAME:-}" ]; then
              echo "No Docker Hub credentials — skipping login (snapshot builds do not push)."
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "$DOCKER_HUB_PASSWORD" | docker login --username "$DOCKER_HUB_USERNAME" --password-stdin

  store_results:
    steps:
      - store_test_results:
          path: ./test-reports

executors:
  linux:
    machine:
      image: ubuntu-2604:current
    resource_class: large.gen3

  # Arm64 counterpart to `linux`, for checking both halves of a multi-arch
  # image. Deliberately small: it only pulls and runs a container.
  linux-arm:
    machine:
      image: ubuntu-2604:current
    resource_class: arm.medium

  macos:
    macos:
      xcode: 26.5.0

  windows:
    machine: true
    resource_class: windows.medium

jobs:
  check:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - run: task ci:check
      - store_results

  test:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - setup
      - run: task ci:test
      - store_results

  mark-release:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Plan deployment
          command: |
            circleci run release plan "${CIRCLE_JOB}" \
              --environment-name="default" \
              --component-name="${CIRCLE_PROJECT_REPONAME}" \
              --target-version="1.0.${CIRCLE_BUILD_NUM}-${CIRCLE_SHA1:0:7}"
      - run:
          name: Update deployment status to running
          command: circleci run release update "${CIRCLE_JOB}" --status=RUNNING
      - run:
          name: Update deployment status to success
          command: circleci run release update "${CIRCLE_JOB}" --status=SUCCESS
          when: on_success
      - run:
          name: Update deployment status to failed
          command: circleci run release update "${CIRCLE_JOB}" --status=FAILED
          when: on_fail

  deploy:
    executor: linux
    parameters:
      publish_steps:
        type: steps
        default:
          - run: task ci:release
    steps:
      - setup
      - setup-docker
      - run: sudo apt update --yes
      - run:
          name: Install snapcraft
          command: |
            sudo apt install snapd --yes
            sudo snap install snapcraft --classic
      - run:
          name: Install choco
          command: |
            sudo cp tools/choco.sh /usr/local/bin/choco
            sudo chmod +x /usr/local/bin/choco
            choco help
      - steps: << parameters.publish_steps >>
      - store_artifacts:
          path: dist

  smoke-test:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
      install-steps:
        type: steps
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - steps: << parameters.install-steps >>
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci binary
          command: circleci version

  # Matrixed over the executors rather than over the tags: only the architecture
  # needs a machine of its own, so each job checks both variants. Printing the
  # arch inside the container makes the log say which half of the manifest ran. A
  # tag missing this platform fails here anyway — the arm machine images carry no
  # binfmt, so there is nothing to silently emulate an amd64-only image with.
  smoke-test-docker:
    parameters:
      executor:
        type: executor
    executor: << parameters.executor >>
    steps:
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci/circleci-cli:v1
          command: docker run --rm circleci/circleci-cli:v1 sh -c 'uname -m; circleci version'
      - run:
          name: Verify circleci/circleci-cli:v1-alpine
          command: docker run --rm circleci/circleci-cli:v1-alpine sh -c 'uname -m; circleci version'

  docs:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - run:
          name: Generate reference and build the site
          command: task docs:build
      - run:
          name: Check internal links
          command: task docs:test
      - store_artifacts:
          path: docs/website/public
      - persist_to_workspace:
          root: .
          paths:
            - "docs/website/public"

  docs-publish:
    executor: linux
    steps:
      - setup
      - attach_workspace:
          at: .
      - run:
          name: Publish to gh-pages
          command: task ci:docs:publish

  ok-to-deploy:
    type: no-op

workflows:
  ci:
    jobs:
      # gh-pages holds only generated HTML — never run CI on it. Entry jobs (no
      # `requires`) must opt out explicitly; downstream jobs are gated by these.

      - check:
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - test:
          matrix:
            parameters:
              executor:
                - linux
                - macos
                - windows
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - docs:
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore: gh-pages

      - deploy:
          name: dry-run
          publish_steps:
            - run: task ci:build
          filters:
            branches:
              ignore:
                - main
                - gh-pages

      - ok-to-deploy:
          requires:
            - check
            - test
            - docs
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - mark-release:
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy

      - deploy:
          serial-group: << pipeline.project.slug >>/deploy
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy
          context:
            - devex-release
            - macos-codesigning

      - docs-publish:
          serial-group: << pipeline.project.slug >>/docs-publish
          requires:
            - ok-to-deploy
          context:
            - devex-release

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-snap
          executor: linux
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install snapd
                command: sudo apt update --yes && sudo apt install snapd --yes
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Snap stable channel
                # /snap/bin has to be prepended, not just present: the machine
                # image ships its own circleci in /usr/local/bin, which would
                # otherwise shadow the snap and make this job verify the build
                # agent's CLI instead of the release.
                command: |
                  sudo snap install circleci
                  echo 'export PATH="/snap/bin:$PATH"' >> "$BASH_ENV"
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-brew
          executor: macos
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Homebrew preview tap
                command: |
                  brew update
                  rm -f /opt/homebrew/bin/circleci
                  brew install circleci-public/circleci/circleci@next
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test-docker:
          matrix:
            parameters:
              executor:
                - linux
                - linux-arm
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

      - smoke-test:
          name: smoke-test-choco
          executor: windows
          install-steps:
            - run:
                name: Install circleci via Chocolatey
                command: choco install circleci-cli -y
          requires:
            - deploy
          filters:
            branches:
              only: main

# CircleCI CLI

Work with CircleCI from the command line.

## Usage

`circleci [flags]`

## CI Commands

| Command      | Description                                      |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `artifact`   | List and download a job's artifact files         |
| `config`     | Generate, validate, process and pack config YAML |
| `job`        | Inspect a job's details, output and artifacts    |
| `pipeline`   | Define what will happen in a run                 |
| `run`        | Trigger, watch and cancel CI runs                |
| `testresult` | Inspect test results for a job                   |
| `workflow`   | Inspect, rerun and cancel workflows (job graphs) |

## Management Commands

| Command             | Description                                            |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------ |
| `certificate`       | Manage iOS code signing certificates                   |
| `component-version` | Manage deploy component versions                       |
| `context`           | Manage secret env vars shared across pipelines         |
| `deploy`            | Track released components and versions                 |
| `dlc`               | Purge a project's Docker layer cache (DLC)             |
| `envvar`            | List, set and delete a project's environment variables |
| `namespace`         | Manage the org namespace orbs publish under            |
| `orb`               | Create, publish and inspect orbs (reusable config)     |
| `org`               | Manage CircleCI organizations                          |
| `policy`            | Govern config with Rego security policies              |
| `project`           | List, follow and configure CircleCI projects           |
| `runner`            | Manage self-hosted runners                             |
| `signing-config`    | Manage iOS signing configs                             |

## User Commands

| Command      | Description                                             |
| ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `auth`       | Log in, sign up and check your CircleCI identity        |
| `completion` | Install, remove or print shell completions              |
| `mcp`        | Run the CLI as an MCP server for AI tools               |
| `my`         | Show resources for the authenticated user               |
| `onboard`    | Guided onboarding: scan, test, generate config, sign up |
| `setting`    | Configure the CLI itself (token, host, defaults)        |

## Extension Commands

| Command     | Description                    |
| ----------- | ------------------------------ |
| `extension` | Manage CLI extensions          |
| `testsuite` | Extension (circleci-testsuite) |

## Additional Commands

| Command   | Description                         |
| --------- | ----------------------------------- |
| `api`     | Call the CircleCI REST API directly |
| `env`     | Work with environment variables     |
| `version` | Print version information           |

## Help Topics

| Topic             | Description                                                   |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `environment`     | Environment variables that can be used with circleci          |
| `formatting`      | Formatting options for JSON data exported from circleci       |

| `reference`       | A comprehensive reference of all circleci commands            |
| `telemetry`       | Information about telemetry in circleci                       |
| `triggers`        | Event source providers and event presets for project triggers |

| Flag                  | Description                                                  |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `-c, --config string` | Path to config file (default: ~/.config/circleci/config.yml) |
| `--debug`             | Enable debug logging                                         |

- Use `circleci <command> <subcommand> --help` for more information about a command.
- Read the manual at <https://cli.circleci.com/reference/>
- Support at <https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/issues>

List recent runs for a project

## Usage

`circleci run list [flags]`

Aliases: `circleci run ls`

## Flags

| Flag                   | Description                                                                       |
| ---------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `-b, --branch string`  | Filter by branch                                                                  |
| `-B, --current-branch` | Filter by the currently checked-out branch                                        |
| `--jq string`          | Process values from the response using jq syntax (see `circleci help formatting`) |
| `--json`               | Output as JSON                                                                    |
| `--limit int`          | Maximum number of runs to show [default: 10] (default 10)                         |
| `--project string`     | Project slug (e.g. gh/org/repo); defaults to git remote                           |

Global flags: `-c, --config`, `--debug`, `--no-color`, `-q, --quiet` — see `circleci --help`.

## Examples

- List recent runs for the current project: 
  `circleci run list`
- Filter to the branch you have checked out: 
  `circleci run list --current-branch`
- Filter to a specific branch: 
  `circleci run list --branch main`
- List runs for an explicit project: 
  `circleci run list --project gh/org/repo`
- Show more results: 
  `circleci run list --limit 25`
- Output as JSON for scripting: 
  `circleci run list --json`

## Details

List recent runs for a CircleCI project.

The project is inferred from the current git repository's remote
unless overridden with --project. Use --branch to filter results
to a single branch, or --current-branch (-B) to automatically use
the branch you have checked out.

The markdown table includes the commit subject; the JSON adds the full
commit and repository detail.

JSON fields: id, phase, outcome, current_outcome, branch, tag, revision, repository_url, commit.subject/url/author_name/author_login, created_at

version: '3'

vars:
  RESULTS_DIR: test-reports
  TEST_REPORT: test-reports/tests.xml
  LINT_REPORT: test-reports/lint.xml

  # Hugo project lives in docs/website/; built output lands in docs/website/public.
  SITE_DIR: docs/website
  SITE_OUT: docs/website/public

  GH_NAME: 'circleci'
  GH_EMAIL: 'ops+deploy-bot@circleci.com'

  # Release version. Every merge to main tags and publishes, so the patch
  # component is the CI build number: unique and monotonically increasing
  # without any manual bookkeeping. Bump RELEASE_SERIES for a minor or major
  # release — 1.1.<build> sorts above every 1.0.<build> under semver.
  #
  # No pre-release suffix: these are full releases, marked latest on GitHub and
  # published to the stable channel of every package manager.
  RELEASE_SERIES: '1.0'
  RELEASE_VERSION: 'v{{.RELEASE_SERIES}}.{{env "CIRCLE_BUILD_NUM" | default "0"}}'

tasks:
  build:
    desc: Build the circleci binary
    vars:
      DEST: '{{default "dist/circleci" .DEST}}'
      COMMIT:
        sh: git rev-parse --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo unknown
      DIRTY:
        sh: test -z "$(git status --porcelain 2>/dev/null)" || echo .dirty
      VERSION: '1.0.0-dev+{{.COMMIT}}{{.DIRTY}}'
    cmds:
      - go build -ldflags="-X main.version={{.VERSION}}" -o "{{.DEST}}" ./cmd/circleci

  release-check:
    desc: Check if the release is ready to be published
    cmds:
      - go tool -modfile tools/go.mod goreleaser check

  test:
    desc: Run unit tests
    # clikit is a separate module, so ./... does not reach it. A relative
    # ./clikit/... is rejected as outside the main module, but the module path
    # resolves through the replace in go.mod.
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "./... github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli/clikit/..." .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - go tool -modfile tools/go.mod gotestsum -- -race -count=1 {{.ARGS}}

  check:
    desc: Run all static checks
    cmds:
      - task: fmt
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: ./... --diff
      - task: fmt:clikit
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: ./... --diff
      - task: lint
      - task: lint:clikit
      - task: license
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: -check .
      - task: mod-tidy
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: -diff
      - task: release-check

  fix:
    desc: Auto-fix static checks
    cmds:
      - task: fmt
      - task: fmt:clikit
      - task: license
      - task: mod-tidy
      - task: lint
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: ./... --fix
      - task: lint:clikit
        vars:
          CLI_ARGS: ./... --fix

  lint:
    desc: Run golangci-lint
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "./..." .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - go tool -modfile tools/go.mod golangci-lint run {{.ARGS}}

  lint:clikit:
    desc: Run golangci-lint on the clikit module
    dir: clikit
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "./..." .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - go tool -modfile ../tools/go.mod golangci-lint run {{.ARGS}}

  fmt:
    desc: Format the code
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "./..." .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - go tool -modfile tools/go.mod golangci-lint fmt {{.ARGS}}

  fmt:clikit:
    desc: Format the clikit module
    dir: clikit
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "./..." .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - go tool -modfile ../tools/go.mod golangci-lint fmt {{.ARGS}}

  license:
    desc: Manage license headers
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "." .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - |
        go tool -modfile tools/go.mod addlicense \
          -c "Circle Internet Services, Inc." \
          -l mit \
          -s \
          -ignore ".idea/**" \
          -ignore ".circleci/**" \
          -ignore ".claude/**" \
          -ignore ".git/**" \
          -ignore ".github/**" \
          -ignore "test-reports/**" \
          -ignore "**/*.html" \
          -ignore "acceptance/testdata/**" \
          -ignore "bin/**" \
          -ignore "dist/**" \
          -ignore "docs/website/content/**" \
          -ignore "docs/website/public/**" \
          {{.ARGS}}

  mod-tidy:
    desc: Run 'go mod tidy'
    vars:
      ARGS: '{{default "-v" .CLI_ARGS}}'
    cmds:
      - go mod tidy {{.ARGS}}
      - go -C clikit mod tidy {{.ARGS}}
      - go -C tools mod tidy {{.ARGS}}

  mod-download:
    desc: Run 'go mod download'
    cmds:
      - go mod download
      - go -C clikit mod download
      - go mod download -modfile tools/go.mod

  dev-install:
    desc: Build from source and install to ~/.local/bin
    vars:
      DEST: '${HOME}/.local/bin'
    cmds:
      - mkdir -p "{{.DEST}}"
      - task: build
        vars:
          DEST: '{{.DEST}}/circleci'

  generate:
    desc: Run go generate
    cmds:
      - go generate ./...

  # Demo tasks
  #
  # Static PNG/SVG screenshots of the CLI in action are captured with
  # charmbracelet/freeze. Animated GIFs are recorded with charmbracelet/vhs
  # (pinned in tools/go.mod alongside freeze), which additionally needs ttyd,
  # ffmpeg, and the demo font at record time — run `task demo:install` once
  # to install them.
  #
  # The vhs tapes in docs/demos/*.tape run the freshly built dist/circleci
  # against real data, so record while logged in — each tape's header comment
  # explains any per-tape prep (e.g. logging out first for auth-login, or
  # substituting a real run id).

  demo:
    desc: Generate all README/docs screenshots
    cmds:
      - task: demo:run-get-png

  demo:run-get-png:
    desc: Capture a macOS-style PNG and SVG of `circleci run get -b main`
    cmds:
      - for: ['svg']
        cmd: >-
          CIRCLE_NO_PAGER=1 CIRCLE_SPINNER_DISABLED=1
          go tool -modfile tools/go.mod freeze
          --config docs/demos/freeze.json
          --execute "go run ./cmd/circleci run get -b main"
          --execute.timeout 60s
          --output docs/demos/run-get.{{.ITEM}}

  demo:install:
    desc: Install the recording dependencies for the VHS demos (ttyd, ffmpeg, JetBrains Mono)
    cmds:
      - brew install ttyd ffmpeg
      # vhs records in a headless browser, so the demo font must be installed
      # system-wide (the copy bundled inside JetBrains IDEs is not visible to it).
      - brew install --cask font-jetbrains-mono

  demo:gifs:
    desc: Record all animated GIF demos with VHS (requires ttyd + ffmpeg)
    deps: [build]
    cmds:
      - for: ['auth-login', 'run-list-get', 'run-get-tui', 'setting-theme', 'run-get-jq']
        cmd: PATH="$PWD/dist:$PATH" go tool -modfile tools/go.mod vhs docs/demos/{{.ITEM}}.tape

  demo:gif:
    desc: 'Record a single demo tape by name, e.g.: task demo:gif -- run-get-tui'
    deps: [build]
    cmds:
      - PATH="$PWD/dist:$PATH" go tool -modfile tools/go.mod vhs docs/demos/{{.CLI_ARGS}}.tape

  extensions:install:
    desc: Install known official extensions
    cmds:
      - go run ./cmd/circleci extension install testsuite

  docs:reference:
    desc: Generate the reference page from the live command tree
    deps:
      - extensions:install
    cmds:
      - mkdir -p {{.SITE_DIR}}/content/reference {{.SITE_DIR}}/static/img
      # The landing page (/) is a hand-written template; the screenshot it shows
      # is the freeze-captured demo, copied into the site's static tree.
      - cp docs/demos/run-get.svg {{.SITE_DIR}}/static/img/run-get.svg
      # Generate the help-topic bodies once, then derive three artifacts:
      #
      #   static/llms.txt             — the short index llmstxt.org actually
      #                                 describes: getting started (install,
      #                                 authenticate, MCP) plus links out. This
      #                                 file used to be the full dump, which cost
      #                                 an agent ~50k tokens to answer "how do I
      #                                 install this?" — and then sent it to the
      #                                 README anyway. Keep it small.
      #   static/llms-full.txt        — every topic plus the whole command tree,
      #                                 for agents that need command detail.
      #   content/reference/_index.md — the same full body with Hugo front
      #                                 matter, served at /reference.
      #
      # Hugo copies static/ to the site root verbatim. Both .txt files open with
      # an H1 + blockquote summary per the llms.txt spec.
      - |
        GS="$(mktemp)"
        REST="$(mktemp)"
        go run ./cmd/circleci help getting-started > "$GS"
        {
          go run ./cmd/circleci help environment
          echo
          go run ./cmd/circleci help formatting
          echo
          go run ./cmd/circleci help reference
        } > "$REST"

        {
          echo '# CircleCI CLI'
          echo
          echo '> Command-line interface to CircleCI for use in your terminal or scripts. This is the short index: install, authenticate, and links to the full reference.'
          echo
          cat "$GS"
          echo
          echo '## Reference'
          echo
          echo '- [Full command reference](https://cli.circleci.com/llms-full.txt): every command, flag and JSON field, generated from the live command tree. Large — fetch it when you need command detail.'
          echo '- [Command reference on the web](https://cli.circleci.com/reference/): the same content as a browsable page.'
          echo '- [Environment variables](https://cli.circleci.com/reference/#environment): authentication, colour, paging and telemetry. Also `circleci help environment`.'
          echo '- [Output formatting](https://cli.circleci.com/reference/#formatting): `--json`, `--jq` and templates. Also `circleci help formatting`.'
          echo '- [Source, issue tracker and prebuilt binaries](https://github.com/CircleCI-Public/circleci-cli)'
        } > {{.SITE_DIR}}/static/llms.txt

        {
          echo '# CircleCI CLI'
          echo
          echo '> Command-line interface to CircleCI for use in your terminal or scripts. This is the full command reference, generated from the live command tree. The short index is at https://cli.circleci.com/llms.txt'

          DRY_RUN: "true"
      - task: ci:cloudsmith
        vars:

      - task: ci:virustotal

Every step is slower than on Linux (checkout 7s vs 1s, module cache 34s vs 27s, tests 2m19s vs 61s on macOS). The executor is `windows.medium`, compared with `large.gen3` for Linux, so the smaller machine is a likely cause. I haven't proven that.

Per `Taskfile.yml`, the `test` task behind it uses `-race -count=1`: race detection slows tests down, and `-count=1` turns off Go's test result cache, so every test runs every time. In the release run I checked, `deploy` (~67s) and `docs-publish` (~36s) spent almost all their time on setup. Their real steps (`task ci:release` and `Publish to gh-pages`) failed in under a second with exit code 201. That run's workflow durations (54s to 7m44s) are mostly queueing and setup, not work. They'll also run longer once they stop failing immediately. The smoke tests never ran, so I have no timings for them.

## Options to consider (nothing changed)
- Start Windows and macOS sooner, or try a larger Windows resource class.
- Check whether `-count=1` and `-race` need to run on every platform.
- Speed up the module cache: make it smaller, or have jobs that don't compile much (like `docs` and `docs-publish`) skip or narrow the restore.
- Use an image that already has snapcraft installed for `dry-run` and `deploy`.

**Caveat:** these figures come mainly from one recent run plus one `main` run. The latest `test-linux` attempt restored its module cache in 0.1 seconds, which may mean the cache wasn't found. That could explain part of its 2m26s test step, but I didn't confirm it from the logs.
